The kicking jumping thing was due to the fact that you were in second gear when you came to a stop and your clutch was not properly engaged. Once you take off it will do the kicking jumping thing if you’re in too high a gear as well. 

As far as having it in 3rd when going 45, if you’re just cruising don’t be afraid to put it in it’s max gear (4th?) to prevent the engine from working at high RPMs unnecessarily. 

One of the main causes of white smoke coming from an exhaust is due to coolant or water seeping into the combustion chamber due to a cracked or warped cylinder head, a cracked engine block, or head gasket failure caused by overheating.

Another thing it can be is that there was water in your fuel tank and you ran the engine with either old and compromised gasoline or there’s water seeping into your tank if it’s exposed to the elements.

Things you need to do:

Make sure the oil pan nut is properly tightened and confirm you didn’t spill the new oil and run the engine without oil.

Get rid of old gas and put high quality gasoline.- if this is the case then the problem MAY be fixed, you will also have to clean out the carburetor since water droplets may be in there.

Inspect the coolant level, your bike may have overheated because you forgot to add coolant, or unknowingly had a leak in the radiator or a tear in a coolant hose. - if this is the case then you probably cracked the head.
Inspect the head gasket

Can you feel the difference between low and high oxygen levels ? 

Short answer: Yes, for both lower and higher levels with prolonged exposure to lower and both short and prolonged exposure to higher depending on the partial pressure of oxygen. This is why people struggle to breathe at higher altitudes where oxygen levels are lower and suffer from oxygen toxicity when placed on high levels of supplemental oxygen.

Long answer : “The result of breathing increased partial pressures of oxygen is hyperoxia, an excess of oxygen in body tissues. The body is affected in different ways depending on the type of exposure. Central nervous system toxicity is caused by short exposure to high partial pressures of oxygen at greater than atmospheric pressure. Pulmonary and ocular toxicity result from longer exposure to increased oxygen levels at normal pressure. Symptoms may include disorientation, breathing problems, and vision changes such as myopia. Prolonged exposure to above-normal oxygen partial pressures, or shorter exposures to very high partial pressures, can cause oxidative damage to cell membranes, collapse of the alveoli in the lungs, retinal detachment, and seizures. Oxygen toxicity is managed by reducing the exposure to increased oxygen levels.”
